title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Social and Emotional Development
subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following competitive sports is particularly appropriate for promoting cooperation, honesty, and trust within and between teams because of its emphasis on the "spirit of the game" and self-refereeing?
options: touch rugby
team handball
slow-pitch softball
ultimate
questions.explain: Ultimate (Frisbee) is unique in its reliance on the "Spirit of the Game," where players are responsible for calling their own fouls and resolving disputes. This system inherently promotes honesty, respect, and cooperation.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following characteristics is most important in functioning effectively as a natural leader and positive role model in sports and physical education activities?
options: the ability to talk others into a particular course of action in an intentional way
a view of leadership as a process for working with problems that need to be solved
the belief that there are right and wrong responses in each situation and intervention is often necessary
the ability to influence a group toward a particular goal in a nonjudgmental, collaborative way
questions.explain: An effective leader in physical education is a positive role model who encourages teamwork and effort. They create a supportive, collaborative climate where all individuals feel respected and can contribute to a shared goal.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: According to principles of developmental psychology, which of the following best describes why participation in play activities is particularly important to young children's growth and development?
options: Virtually all of what children learn is derived from observing others, thus young children learn how to behave by observing older children at play.
Play settings provide the environments in which children develop the ability to overcome confusion related to appearance versus reality.
Since play provides important information about gender roles, children with limited opportunities to play often experience delayed development of gender identity.
Play allows children to try out and test new physical, cognitive, and social behaviors, which then become part of their working memory.
questions.explain: Play is a primary vehicle for learning in early childhood. It provides a safe, low-stakes environment for children to explore, practice, and internalize new physical, cognitive, and social skills, which is fundamental to their development.

questions.q: Which of the following approaches is likely to be most effective in fostering appropriate attitudes about body composition and body image in children?
options: emphasizing that individuals come in a variety of sizes and shapes within a range of healthy body weights
encouraging children to adopt the eating patterns and dietary choices favored by their family and culture
instructing children how to determine their body mass index and encouraging them to check it often
promoting children's ability to identify and compare variations in individual fitness levels among classmates
questions.explain: A healthy attitude about body image involves recognizing that there is no single ideal body type. Emphasizing the diversity of healthy body shapes and sizes helps children develop self-acceptance and avoid unhealthy comparisons.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Cooperative games and team sports help promote the development of positive traits and values primarily by providing opportunities in which students can:
options: study and emulate the interpersonal skills of a variety of adult role models.
compete against themselves rather than against other individuals.
remain confident and free of worries about the possibility that peers may make fun of them.
observe and practice character-building skills such as determination, loyalty, self-control, and civility.
questions.explain: Working together in cooperative games and team sports provides a practical context for students to learn and apply crucial social skills and character traits like loyalty, self-control, and determination toward a common goal.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Recreational group and team games such as horseshoes, ultimate, and volleyball are especially well suited to providing social benefits to participants primarily because they:
options: keep participants of all fitness levels equally challenged.
require participants to take turns self-officiating.
promote enjoyment and camaraderie among participants with similar interests.
involve competition and scoring, thus generating comments and discussions among participants.
questions.explain: The primary social benefit of these recreational games stems from the shared enjoyment and interaction among people with similar interests. This interaction builds camaraderie and positive social connections.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Following a track meet against a rival team, a student and the physical education teacher discuss the 200 meter. "I can't believe I didn't place first in the 200! I trained so hard during the last two weeks," the student says. "Sorry to see you so disappointed. I know that race was really important to you," the teacher replies. This response is appropriate in this situation primarily because it:
options: provides an objective overview and downplays the loss.
expresses admiration for the student's performance in the race.
affirms that the student set a goal and worked hard.
acknowledges that the teacher knows exactly how much time the student spent preparing for the race.
questions.explain: The teacher's response is empathetic and supportive. By acknowledging the student's disappointment and the importance of the race, the teacher validates the student's feelings and affirms the hard work and goal-setting process, not just the outcome.
